JUDGMENT
The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by her in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
2. That on 02-8-2023 at about 10-20 a.m the petitioner was riding the scooter bearing Reg.No.KA- 04/JS-0457 near Mattikere circle on Bellary road, Sadashivanagar, Bangalore, when she reached Opposite to HQTC gate, at that time, driver of Car bearing Registration No.KA-50/P-0681 drove the same with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the Petitioner's motor cycle, as a result the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

3. It is further stated that immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Manipal Hospital for first aid, then she was shifted to Astra Hospital, wherein she took treatment as an inpatient and spent Rs.4,50,000/- towards her medical expenses, conveyance and nourishment etc.,
and she has to incur future medical expenses also.

4. It is also stated in the petition that, prior to the accident she was working as Chief Admin at RTIPS Techno Pvt., ltd., and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
5.
It is stated that, the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent act of the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-50/P-0681.
In this regard, case was registered against the driver by the jurisdictional Sadashivanagar Traffic Police in Crime No.65/2023 for the offence punishable under section 279 and 338 of IPC.
As such, the respondent No.1 being the insurance company and the respondent No.2 being the owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed the instant petition, seeking compensation.
6. In response to the notices, the respondent No.1 & 2 have appeared through their respective Counsels.
The respondent No.2/R.C. Owner of the offending vehicle has filed the written statement.
On the other hand, the respondent No.1 / Insurance company has not filed it's written statement.
7. In the written statement of the respondent No.2 has stated that, the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts of the case.
Further she has denied the entire case of the petitioner as false.

While admitting about R.C. owner of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-50/P-0681 this respondent stated that, the driver of said vehicle had valid D.L. and she got insured said vehicle with respondent No.1 and policy was in force as on the date of the accident, hence the respondent No.1 has to indemnify the respondent No.2.
Further she has denied the manner in which the accident took place, injuries sustained, avocation, age and income of the petitioner as false.

It is contended that, the accident Hemalatha S vs Universal Sampo Gen Ins Co Ltd on 5 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178866679/
2 occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the petitioner and nature of injuries are simple in nature as per her own statement before jurisdictional Police.

sentences.text: It is also the contention of the respondent No.1 that the compensation and interest claimed by the petitioner is exorbitant.
Upon these grounds, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

8. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the parties, this court has framed the following:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that she had sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident that was taken place on 2-8-2023 at about 10.20 a.m.
Opp.HQTC Gate, Bellary road, near Mattikere circle, Sadashivanagar, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-50/P-0681 in an actionable negligence?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation as prayed for?

If so, at what rate? from whom?
3) What order or award?

9. In order to substantiate the case of the petitioner, she herself examined as PW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to P22 and placed the evidence of Dr.S.Ramachandra as PW2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P23 & 24.
10.
On the other hand, the respondents have not adduced their evidence.

11. Heard the arguments of both the counsel and perused the materials available on record.
12.

My answer to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.

Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative.
 Issue No.3:

As per final order,
 for the following:
 R E A S O N S ISSUE No.1:-
13.

It is the specific case of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-50/P-0681, the alleged accident had taken place, consequently she had sustained grievous injuries.
14. On the other hand, the respondent No.2 seriously disputed the accident and took sepcific contention that, the accident taken place due to sole negligence on the part of the petitioner.

sentences.text: The petitioner in order to prove her case, examined herself as PW1.
PW1 in her examination- in-chief by way of affidavit has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
The petitioner in support of her oral evidence has relied upon Ex.
P1 to P7
Ex.P1-true copy of the F.I.R. in Crime No.65/2023 of Sadashivanagar Traffic Police Station,
Ex.P2-true copy of the first information statement given by the petitioner.

Ex.P3-true copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P4-true copy of sketch, Ex.P5-true copy of IMV report, Ex.P6-true copies of wound certificate of the petitioner, Ex.P7-true copy of the charge sheet in Crime No.65/2023 of Sadashivanagar Traffic police.

17. On perusal of the police documents, it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement given by the petitioner, the S.H.O. of Sadashivanagar Traffic police has registered the case against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Sections 279 & 338 of IPC.
Upon investigation, the I.O. has filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 338 of IPC.

18. Apart from this, even at the time of cross- examination of PW1, no material answers culled out to believe the defenses of the respondent No.2 about the denial of allegation made against the driver of the offending vehicle.
19. Though the respondent No.2 has filed written statement contending that, the accident was occurred due to sole negligence of the petitioner.
But in this regard she has not placed any oral or documentary evidence, even she has not examined driver of offending vehicle.
Mere denial in written statement does not rebut the case of the petitioner.
20. In the light of evidence placed on record, it is crystal clear that, the alleged accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-50/P-0681.
As such, the petitioner has placed the satisfactory and convincing evidence on record to prove the above issue.
Hence, without making much discussion on the point of rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, I am answering the issue No.1, in the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2 :
21.
This issue is with respect to the entitlement of reliefs claimed by the petitioner.
The petitioner through this petition, claiming compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- on account of the injuries sustained by her in the accident under different heads.

22. Before appreciation of the evidence placed by the petitioner about the injuries sustained by her in the accident and its consequences, it is apt to note herein, the preposition laid down in the following land mark judgment, while appreciating the injury cases in Motor Vehicle Act.
Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.

sentences.text: "In the aforesaid case, it was held that, the court has to make judicious attempt to award compensation to the loss suffered by the claimant.
The compensation should not be assessed conservatively.
On the other hand, compensation should also not be endeavouring to secure some uniformity and consistency.
The object of awarding compensation is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done, as far as money can do so, in a fair reasonable and equitable manner."

"while determining quantum of compensation, in such cases, the court has to strike a balance between the inflated and unreasonable demands of a victim and the equally untenable claim of the opposite party saying that nothing is payable.
That sympathy for the victim does not, and should not, comes in the way of making a correct assessment.
But if a case is made out, and the court must not be chary of awarding adequate compensation."

Pain and Sufferings;
23.
PW1 has stated in her evidence that, she has sustained the injuries in a road traffic accident.
In connection with the injuries she has produced wound certificate marked as Ex.P6.

The said document discloses that, she had sustained the following injuries:-
1. left arm muscle deep laceration with deformity 2. left ankle talus dislocation with tendon injury with comminuted lateral malleolus fracture 3. Multiple abrasins over face, right foot and left knee.
24.
In connection with the above said injuries, the doctor is of the opinion that the injury No.3 is simple in nature and injury No. 1 and 2 are grievous in nature.
Further, the petitioner has produced two discharge summaries per Ex.P8 & P9.
On going through the discharge summary Ex.P8 issued by Astra Super Specialty Hospital, the petitioner was admitted on 02-08-2023 and discharged on 06-08- 2023.
Another discharge summary Ex
. P9 shows that the petitioner was admitted on 06-09-2023 and discharged on 08-09-2023.
In addition to her evidence, placed the evidence of Dr.S.Ramachandra as PW2.

PW2 has placed outpatient recrod, three X- rays and clinical examination note as per Ex.P23 &
24.

By taking into consideration of the nature of the injuries and the treatment taken by the petitioner, she might have undergone pain and sufferings while taking treatment, as an inpatient as well as an outpatient.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.50,000/- under the head of Pain and Sufferings.

Loss of income during treatment period:
25.
PW1 has stated that, she was working as Chief Admin at RTIPS Techno Pvt., Ltd., and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
In support of her case, she has placed offer letter, pay slips, bank statement, which are marked at Ex.P13 to Ex.P16.

On perusal of pay slips marked at Ex.P14 the petitioner was getting Hemalatha S vs Universal Sampo Gen Ins Co Ltd on 5 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178866679/
5

After deducting Rs.200/- professional tax, it comes to Rs.24,800/-
per month.

On going through the discharge summary issued by Astra Hospital which reveals that the petitioner was admitted on 02-08-2023 and discharged on 06-08-2023 and again dmitted on 06- 09-2023 and discharged on 08-09-2023.
During the period of treatment, definitely, there was some difficulty to her to do daily routine work at least for a period of one month by looking in to the nature of the injuries sustained by her.
Hence, I am of the view that, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.24,800/- towards loss of income during the laid up period and rest period.

Medical Expeneses;
26.
The petitioner in connection with her treatment expenses, at the time of her evidence, placed medical bills as per Ex.P20.
Out of total bill amount in Sl.No.1 bill, it is raised for Rs.34,007/-.
PW.1 in her cross examination has stated that, she had paid the said bill amount.
Sl.No.2 bill is raised for Rs.2,47,236/-.
Out of it, Star health insurance company has paid Rs.2,05,977/- and Rs.12,395/- is given as discount.
Further, admissible amount is Rs.2,05,977.

Other deductions is Rs.28,864/-
which was paid by the petitioner.
Sl . No.3
bill is raised for Rs.1,27,940/- only admissible amount is Rs.1,19,318/- which is paid by Star Health insurance.
PW1 in her cross examination has admitted that the Star Health insurance has paid Rs.2,05,977/- to the hospital.
Further, the said bills disclose that Star health insurance company has paid Rs.2,05,977/- and Rs.1,19,398/-.
Therefore the petiitoner is not entilted for riembursement of medical bills paid by the star health insurance company.
Sl.No.4 to 33 bills are raised for medicine bills and also ambulance charges which amount for Rs.55,866/-.
After deducting ambulance bills of Rs.30,500/-, it comes to Rs.25,366/-.
There are no any contradictios to disbelieve the other bills produced by the petitioner.
Thus the petitioner is entitled for medical bills of Rs.34,007/-, Rs.28,864/- and Rs.25,366/-.
In total Rs.88,237/- and same is awarded towards medical expenses.

Attendant charges, food and nourishment and conveyance charges;
27.
As per the medical records and also on going through the discharge summaries the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient.
During that period, definitely the petitioner might have spent some amount towards, food, nourishment, conveyance, as well as towards attendant charges.
The petitoiner has produced Ex.P19, house keeping bill for amount of Rs.1,25,000/-.
Further the petitioner has produced ambulance bills of Rs.30,500/-.
But for Rs.20,000/- there is no seal of the said ambulance service.
But, she has not examined the author of said bills.
Therefore, by considering the injuries sustained by the petitoner, this tribunal awarded reasonable compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards attendant charges, food, nourishment and conveyance charges.

Loss of future income;
28.
The petitioner herein asserting that, she had sustained permanent disability, consequent upon the injuries sustained by her.
In order to prove the same, the petitioner has relied on her evidence along with the wound certificate and other medical documents.

In the evidence of the PW1,
reiterated the same thing forthcoming in the main petition.

As already discussed above, wound certificate placed by her as per Ex.P6 goes to show that, she had sustained two grievous injuries, for Hemalatha S vs Universal Sampo Gen Ins Co Ltd on 5 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178866679/

sentences.text: To substantiate this, the petitioner had placed discharge summaries for consideration.
Apart from this, another material witness by name Dr.Ramachandra examined as PW2.

PW2 has stated in his evidence that the petitioner has sustained left ankle talus dislocation with tendon injury with comminuted lateral malleolus fracture and left humerus comminuted fracture of shaft.

Further stated that, the petitioner has undergone:
open reduction + K wire fixation + tendon repair done to talus and ORIF (open reduction internal fixation) with titanium LCP (locking compression plate) and screws done to fracture of left humerus on 2-8-2023 and discharged on 6-8-2023.

Second admission on date 6-9-2023 and she has GAP at humerus fracture with implants in situ and undergone operation of radial nerve neurolysis + bone graft taken from iliac crest and fixed to left humerus, ORIF done for left ankle fracture on 7-9-2023 and discharged on 8-9- 2023.
Further he has assessed the disability to the upper limb at 15.28% and whole body disability at 16%, contributed by left lower limb + 15.28% by left upper limb = 31.28%.

He has placed clinical note with outpatient record and x-rays, which are marked as per Ex.P23 &
Ex.P24.
29.
At the time of cross-examination of PW3, admitted that he is not treated doctor.
Further admitted that comminuted fracture shaft of left humerus was not united and comminuted fracture of lateral malleolus of left ankle was united.
This witness also denied the suggestion that, he assessed the disability of the petitioner in higher side.
30. PW1 has stated that she was working as a Chief Admin at RTIPS Pvt. Ltd., and was drawing salary of Rs.25,000/- per month.
She has placed offer letter, pay slips, bank statement, which are marked at Ex.P13 to Ex.P16.
On perusal of pay slips marked at Ex.P14 the petitioner was getting salary of Rs.25,000/- per month.
On perusal of Ex.P16 it reveals that she has not attended the office till the date.
In the cross examination she has admitted that she has continued her service, still she is getting salary of Rs.25,000/- per month.
31. In such a situation, question of loss of future income does not arise all.
At the same time, it is to be noted that, due to the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner, there would be some difficulty to her to do normal work, as she was earlier.

Hence, I relied the decision reported in, ILR 2015 KAR 167 in between Dr.Yashawanth Dongre Vs. Salman Rasheed and Others, it was observed,
that.

entities.text: Dr.Yashawanth Dongre Vs. Salman Rasheed and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "The claimant has got disability to the extent of 46%.
The doctor has not spoken about the disability with regard to the whole body.

The claimant has permanent disability and thus has permanent diminution of his earning capacity, but he has been continued in the same employment without deduction of salary, the claimant is entitled for compensation for his handicap in the labor market.
In many cases of comparatively not serious injuries, though there is some permanent disability, the disability has no immediate adverse effect on his salary.
He may be getting the pre-accident salary.
However, such a man is at a disadvantage when compared with his co-workers in the labour market.

It may so happen that he continues to work with difficulty and gets the same salary but if there is reduction in the workforce by the employers, this worker with disability is likely to be sent off first."

sentences.text: On perusal of the above said decision, it is observed that, though the claimant is in a position to work physically after the accident as before, the after effects of the accident may make it more difficult for him to find work or to retain his work.
There would be some degree of physical handicap.
Since the claimant is continuing his employment, he may be entitled for compensation under the head of reduced eligibility of employment.
In this regard, a suitable sum has to be awarded by way of damages, having regard to his disability.

33. In the instant case, on going through the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and also on going through the evidence given by the doctor in connection with the disability of the petitioner, I am of the view that, though the petitioner has continued her job, she has to suffer with the said disability throughout her life and the eligibility of her employment has been reduced due to the disability sustained by her, in a road traffic accident.
So, suitable sum has to be awarded by way of damages having regard to her disability.

Considering the above facts, I am of the view that, it is just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.1,50,000/- under the head of reduced eligibility of employment or damages due to disability.

Loss of amenities;
34.
As noted above, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the accident as a result she has permanent partial disability.
The petitioner was aged about 43 years at the time of the accident.

The said disability certainly affects not only on her avocation, but also affects on her amenities as the petitioner could not able to enjoy her life as she was enjoying earlier prior to the accident.
By overall considering these aspects it is just and proper to award Rs.20,000/- towards loss of amenities.

35. In connection with the future medication, PW2 has stated that the petitioner has to undergo two more operations for correction of non-union of fracure shaft of left humorous and removal of implants from lateral malleolus of left ankle and attending to left ankle joint bone (Talus) and to do operation depending upon severity of osteoarthritis.
Neither the petitioner nor the doctor have not produced the estimation for future medication.

However, having considering the escalation of rates in all the fields even including in medical field, this tribunal is of opinion that, it is proper to award Rs.40,000/- under the head future medical expenses.

36. In view of my discussions held above, on various aspects the petitioner is entitled for compensation in to to, under the following heads:

LIABILITY:
38.

As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Car bearing Registration No.KA-50/P-0681,
alleged accident had taken place.
The evidence given by the petitioner in connection with the issue No.1, remained unshaken.

As such, it is the strong assertion of the petitioner that, the respondent No.1 being the insurer and the respondent No.2 being the RC owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
39. As per the records insurance policy was valid from 19.11.2022 to 18.11.2023.
The alleged accident had taken place on 02.08.2023.

The respondent No.1 though appeared through its counsel,
but inspite of granting sufficient time, they have not filed written statement to disprove the contention of the petitioner.

As such, I am of the view that, the respondent No.1 being the Insurer and the respondent No.2 being the RC owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
However, the respondent No.1, being the insurance company and indemnifier has to satisfy the award.
In view of the valid insurance policy, the respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition, till its realization.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
40.

In view of above discussions on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,93,037/- (Rupees three lakh ninety three thousand and thirty seven only) along with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of the petition till the realization of the award amount.
The respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioner.

In view of valid insurance policy the respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realisation within two months from the date of this order.
The expenses to be incurred for future medication shall not carry any interest.

The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by her in a road traffic accident.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
17. On perusal of the police documents, it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement given by the petitioner, the S.H.O. of Sadashivanagar Traffic police has registered the case against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Sections 279 & 338 of IPC.
Upon investigation, the I.O. has filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 338 of IPC.
18. Apart from this, even at the time of cross- examination of PW1, no material answers culled out to believe the defenses of the respondent No.2 about the denial of allegation made against the driver of the offending vehicle.
19. Though the respondent No.2 has filed written statement contending that, the accident was occurred due to sole negligence of the petitioner.
But in this regard she has not placed any oral or documentary evidence, even she has not examined driver of offending vehicle.
Mere denial in written statement does not rebut the case of the petitioner.
20. In the light of evidence placed on record, it is crystal clear that, the alleged accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-50/P-0681.
As such, the petitioner has placed the satisfactory and convincing evidence on record to prove the above issue.

7 32.
Since the claimant is continuing his employment, he may be entitled for compensation under the head of reduced eligibility of employment.
In this regard, a suitable sum has to be awarded by way of damages, having regard to his disability.
33. In the instant case, on going through the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and also on going through the evidence given by the doctor in connection with the disability of the petitioner, I am of the view that, though the petitioner has continued her job, she has to suffer with the said disability throughout her life and the eligibility of her employment has been reduced due to the disability sustained by her, in a road traffic accident.
So, suitable sum has to be awarded by way of damages having regard to her disability.
Considering the above facts, I am of the view that, it is just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.1,50,000/- under the head of reduced eligibility of employment or damages due to disability.
Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,93,037/- (Rupees three lakh ninety three thousand and thirty seven only) along with interest @ 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Honourable High court of Karnataka in, MFA No.103557/2016,
between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S. Lakshmi And Others dated. 20.03.2018.
And MFA No.30131/2019 dated.12.5.2020, from the date of the petition, till the realization of the award amount.
As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Car bearing Registration No.KA-50/P-0681,
alleged accident had taken place.
As such, it is the strong assertion of the petitioner that, the respondent No.1 being the insurer and the respondent No.2 being the RC owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
The alleged accident had taken place on 02.08.2023.
As such, I am of the view that, the respondent No.1 being the Insurer and the respondent No.2 being the RC owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,93,037/- (Rupees three lakh ninety three thousand and thirty seven only) along with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of the petition till the realization of the award amount.
The respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioner.
In view of valid insurance policy the respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realisation within two months from the date of this order.
The expenses to be incurred for future medication shall not carry any interest.
After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, entire amount shall be released to the petitioner through due process of law as she had incurred huge amount for her medical expenses and also she has to incur some more amount towards her future medication.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
